label: sparse: <DEL> / first copy step of long sequences (combinatorial, uncaptured)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps, max 0.25). About 59% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> step or the first copy step (recall_idx 0-1), mostly with L=8-9; it is nearly silent in the original phase and never fires before t=6. Inside that window it fires on well under 1% of steps. Which steps fire depends on a combination of sequence contents: enrichment for first token b/u, out_tok in {v,e,u,q}, next_out in {x,v,w,l}, and l at position 2 / 0 at position 4 in top examples. None of these, alone or combined, gets precision above ~7%. The remaining ~40% of mass is scattered over later copy steps, often on input b or 3. Best predicate F1 was below 0.07.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: b, u, m, 3, v, j; least: r, y, 2, c) and the third original token (most: l, x, v, w, m, 3; least: a, y, g, f); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=8, L=9.
